notes.2: In this question about a speed-time graph candidates had to spot that the gradient, and hence the acceleration, were zero at 40 s. Many candidates opted for B, which would give the mean value of acceleration from 3 m/s to 15 m/s over 40 s.
notes.3: A common error here was to believe that runner 2 was slowing down, confusing reducing acceleration with reducing speed.
notes.4: This question concerned the forces on a satellite orbiting the Earth at constant speed, and a number of candidates thought that the resultant force on it must act in its instantaneous direction of travel and so chose option C.
notes.13: This question concerned a barometer, and a significant proportion of candidates believed that the space above the column of mercury would increase in length and so selected option A.
notes.18: Virtually all candidates were aware that the black car would show the greater temperature increase, but approximately half of these also thought that the white car would show the greater decrease, therefore choosing option B.
notes.20: The mistake made by many weaker candidates here was to fail to convert kHz to Hz, leading to option C.
notes.26: Weaker candidates often opted for A for this question, confusing magnetic and electric fields.
notes.28: Although a large proportion of candidates could calculate the current in this question, a significant number chose the wrong direction for electron flow.
notes.30: The most common mistake here was to choose B, not appreciating that the current would not be rectified.
notes.32: In this question on an LDR in a potential divider circuit, option B was popular among weaker candidates, indicating a lack of appreciation of the effect of light level on the resistance of an LDR, as well as an incorrect understanding of the effect of decreased resistance on the p.d. across the LDR.
notes.33: The most common mistake here was to think that a fuse would reduce the current to its rated value.
notes.36: Only the strongest candidates were able to select the correct answer to this question on deflection of β- particles.
notes.37: This question concerned an application of a radioactive source, which proved challenging for many candidates with only the strongest answering correctly.
notes.general_comments: Many candidates coped well with this new multiple choice paper.
